knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Asking how the person prefers to be addressed, using approved interpreters where needed and checking understanding without patronising shows respectful communication. The procedure asks for preferred forms of address, clear short explanations and no patronising language. A loud voice for everyone, assumptions from language or background, and speaking to a family member instead of the client all fail this.

Pausing the affected work, checking directly with the person and reporting the uncertainty to the designated contact is correct. Where consent is unclear the task is paused and the designated coordinator is contacted. Asking for a signature and proceeding, sharing confidential details or guessing the answer do not resolve the uncertainty.
The workplace procedure says to use approved interpreters or communication supports when required, and not to assume family members may receive confidential information.

practicalCriteria: Adapts communication respectfully, checks understanding and safeguards confidential information.
Recognises and escalates unsafe or out-of-scope work
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Record of procedure step 7: If the task goes beyond your training, the consent given, safe access or the agreed scope, pause the affected work, report it promptly and document the reason.
Record of procedure step 8: Record agreed preferences only in authorised systems, without unnecessary personal detail.
stopWorkCriteria: Stop work if procedure step 5 is not done: Do not pass confidential information to family members on assumption, and check consent first.
Stop work if procedure step 6 is not done: Before acting, confirm your authorisation, the hazards, and who handles escalation.
